threads.body: [General] This does not actually create the agent-side bound counter. The returned wrapper calls the ordinary `add(value, attributes)` path on every recording, so it still performs the attribute processing and timeseries lookup that the 1.65 `bind` contract explicitly eliminates. Bind the agent `ExtendedLongCounter` once and have the application wrapper delegate to its `BoundLongCounter` (retaining a fallback only if an agent implementation lacks the incubator API).

[General] This emulates binding by retaining attributes and then using the unbound `add(value, attributes)` path for every update. That forfeits the cached-timeseries behavior promised by the 1.65 bound-instrument API. Bind the agent `ExtendedDoubleCounter` here and delegate through its `BoundDoubleCounter`, with a fallback only when the agent implementation does not expose the incubator interface.

replies.body:
Addressed in daf6b7c5ecf7a13a6e1b2972e0b479c245ad2202.

Analysis: All eight application-side bind implementations converted attributes once but retained an unbound agent instrument, so every update still repeated attribute processing and timeseries lookup. The bound wrapper factories now detect the corresponding agent Extended interface, invoke bind once, and retain primitive delegates to the agent Bound instrument for both implicit and explicit context updates. Plain agent instruments retain the previous unbound path as a compatibility fallback.

Upsides: Restores the cached-timeseries semantics of the 1.65 bound metric API across counters, up/down counters, histograms, and gauges; preserves explicit context bridging; and remains compatible with agent instrument implementations that do not expose incubator interfaces.

Downsides: Each bind allocates two primitive delegate objects, and implementations without the agent incubator API continue to use the less efficient fallback path.
